## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of the integrate+decide loop with a mask-based respawn scan can approach the streaming ceiling.

## Layout & approach
The AoS layout at 69 B/p (68 B struct + 1 B mask) offers 41% hot bytes for loop 1 (age+pos+vel = 28 B) and only 5% for loop 2 (seed = 4 B); the rest is dead weight in every line. The mask intermediate (1 B/p) is written in loop 1 and scanned in a non-Halide-expressible loop 2. With 69 B/p the working set spills L1d at N≈474 and L2 at N≈7598, so most measured points sit in L2 or deeper, dragging 59% dead bytes through each level.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p is nearly flat: 21.6 (L1d, N=320) through 21.9–23.6 (L2) and 24.2–24.6 (L3), rising to 26.7 at DRAM (N=10M) — 24% total with no sharp spill knee. The L1d→L2 transition is invisible. Higher death rates steepen the DRAM penalty: q=0.1 jumps from 25.4 (L3) to 31.1 (DRAM), q=0.25 from 27.7 to 33.4. These transitions are small relative to the absolute cost — the algo is overhead-dominated, not cache-dominated.

## Bandwidth
Achieved 2.2–3.2 GB/s against the 12.69 GB/s ceiling — 17–25%. The memory floor of 5.437 ns/p means the algo runs 4–6× above irreducible memory time: frontend-bound. The profile confirms — frontend_stall 64–72%, backend_stall 0–11%, branch_flush 0%. Ratios vs baseline are 0.93–1.05×: tied with naive scalar. At q=0.01 N=320: 0.975× baseline, 2.911× winner; at q=0.5 N=320: 0.934× baseline, 1.866× winner. The advantage inverts at DRAM: q=0.1 N=10M is 1.168× baseline. The winner (AF02.LP1-autovec.LP2-opt) is 1.85–3.5× faster everywhere.

## Assembly
Loop 1 (L58–L67) uses partial vectorization: `vmovups` loads pos, `vmulps`/`vaddps` do 4-wide FP, but `vmovss` scalar stores and `vinsertps` shuffles break lanes — mixed vec 6 / scalar 6, 9 byte-granular scatters at stride 68B. Loop 2 (L69–L90) is the bottleneck: 485 insns/iter, 98 conditional branches, unrolled 32× with individual `cmp BYTE PTR [r12+r13*1+N],0x0` / `je` / `call spawn` sequences, each preceded by `vzeroupper` (34 total). A `vmovdqu`+`vptest` 32-byte bulk check is the only real vectorization in loop 2. Only 16 of 619 instructions are vector-suffixed — the 64–72% frontend stall is the direct consequence.

## Verdict
Refuted — ties naive (0.93–1.05× baseline) and loses to the winner by 1.85–3.5× at every point. At q=0.01 N=320: 0.975× baseline, 2.911× winner; at q=0.5 N=10M: 1.025× baseline, 1.881× winner. The mechanism is frontend starvation: 64–72% frontend stalls from a 485-instruction, 98-branch respawn loop with 34 `vzeroupper` transitions, achieving only 17–25% of ceiling. The mask scan cannot vectorize, and partial loop-1 vectorization (16/619 vector insns) cannot compensate.
